paragraphs: 弗雷多站了起來，看向冒險者們。是時候準備出發了。羅特露出了複雜的表情，表示自己需要一點時間，他有些人想聊聊。弗雷多告訴冒險者們，最晚得在日落前出發，否則太晚了。羅特找到了賽柏，此刻的賽柏煥然一新，在常翠林，他找到了自己的歸屬。賽柏帶著羅特到了基地的一間儲藏間，拉了兩把椅子，確保這裡是個舒服的談話空間，不被打擾。

羅特向賽柏訴說了自從出來冒險後的一路發展，如何從相信蜘蛛神、遭母親大人背叛、轉向愛神利希恩，然後一路走到現在。羅特覺得，自己似乎總是帶來厄運與災害，走到哪裡都沒有希望，這讓他很痛心，也懷疑自己是不是該先停下來了。賽柏看著羅特，表示這個世界本來就充滿了苦難，就算沒有羅特，這些事情還是會發生，也因此，他希望羅特不要太責怪自己。同時他也表示自己很感激能找到常翠林這個地方，讓他覺得終於有家的感覺。羅特也對於自己的信仰不斷轉換感到困擾，羨慕賽柏能找到像涅西斯這樣「看起來沒什麼問題」的宗教。賽柏則表示，每個宗教都有不同派系，也很難講這個派系沒有任何問題。不過，對於宗教的選擇，他一直以來都只有涅西斯而已，如果羅特的困擾是和換了不同宗教有關，他們身邊那位月神教的信徒，似乎是更好的談話對象。羅特點點頭，和賽柏離開了儲藏間。賽柏拍拍他的肩膀，表示不論他決定怎麼做，都支持他。

羅特找了佛拉，也帶他來到了剛剛的那間儲藏間。椅子還沒收走，正好讓兩人能坐著聊聊。兩人分享了在母親大人屠殺了隊友們後的心境，也得知雙方都從未從中走出，甚至可能一輩子都走不出來。羅特猶豫著接下來該怎麼做？該怎麼走？該繼續冒險，還是該停下來？佛拉表示自己想先停下來，他的身體還沒完全復原，但同時，他也知道常翠林不是他該待的地方，身為月神芬尼爾的信徒，待在這個涅西斯的領地，不會有什麼好事發生。他也鼓勵羅特不要顧及其他人的想法，做自己就對了。羅特說道，自己想先離開團隊一段時間，也覺得好像應該先和他的夥伴們知會一聲，不讓他們擔心。佛拉調皮地笑了笑，說：「如果我們一起偷偷溜走⋯⋯不是很有趣嗎？這是我們的自由，沒有人可以管得著。」羅特點了點頭，兩人小心翼翼地推開儲藏室的門，準備朝後門走去。門一打開，羅特才發現賽柏還在門邊。賽柏表示不用管他，羅特也希望賽柏不要告訴其他人他們在這裡。賽柏點點頭，朝著反方向走了。
羅特與佛拉悄悄地溜到後門，輕輕推開門：夕陽的餘暉正照在一望無際的草皮上。草地上沒有鋪好的路，就像他們的未來，沒有被決定好一樣。羅特愣住了，靜靜看著，然後默默牽起佛拉的手。接著他感覺到一陣拉扯，佛拉已拉著羅特的手，輕快地向前奔去。羅特快步跟上，徜徉著，像是無憂無慮的孩子一樣，逐漸消失在夕陽的另一端。
時間已差不多，但一直不見羅特的蹤影。巴斯正好看見經過的賽柏，便詢問他是否有看見羅特。賽柏表示他有看見羅特和佛拉在儲藏間那邊，但在那之後他就不知道了。眼看再不出發就要來不及了，弗雷多便催促巴斯和烏波上路。烏波的烏鴉飛回到他的身上。先前在儲藏室內，牠躲在羅特的帽兜內，但他選擇不告訴烏波到底發生了什麼事。烏波大概也聽不懂，他想。
弗雷多給了巴斯兩個選項：他們可以步行，會比較慢，但比較不會發現；也可以騎馬，比較快，但從這裡帶走馬可能會被注意到。為了低調，巴斯選擇徒步的選項。
朝著冒險者們來的方向，弗雷多帶著兩人前行。途中，大家再次看見狼人的腳印。弗雷多表示他雖然還沒看過真的狼人，但聽過很多傳聞，因此在這路上需要特別小心。接近午夜，三人找了一棵大樹旁紮營準備進食與休息。弗雷多拿了多帶的乾糧分配給巴斯與烏波當晚餐。三人分配好了守夜的工作後，便輪流休息了。

次日一早，弗雷多與冒險者們吃飽後便出發了。三人繼續往回走，一路上沒有遇到太多的問題，只有中午時暫時停下來休息與補充食糧。途中，巴斯也和弗雷多詢問了關於家族的事。弗雷多表示自己的家族世代侍奉巴斯的家族，但近年來家族內分為兩派：他的父親支持巴斯的父親，對死靈術進行深入研究；非常照顧他的大哥則因為「多做了些研究」，反對他的父親，而弗雷多因為哥哥的關係，也選擇了自己的路線。大約五十年前，他離開了家鄉，來到了常翠林，卻也發現常翠林有他們的對立勢力：他不確定是他父親的勢力，還是甚至與該家族對立。巴斯詢問後，弗雷多也建議到石原鎮後，他們應該去找他的哥哥。想起烏波曾提過看過他的家傳寶物「懷錶」的記憶，巴斯向烏波請求變身成他記憶中那名女子的模樣。烏波化身為記憶中的妖精女子：那是名全身潔白，髮色金黃的貴族女子，身穿青綠色的絲綢，衣服的邊緣鑲著金邊，纏繞成某個像是家徽的符號。巴斯對於這個符號認不得，但以他對家輝設計的認識，這肯定是與他家族勢力相當的家族。

夜裡，當他們準備好找地方紮營時，烏波看見前方一棵大樹下有些微火光。一個人類站著，而地上躺著另一個人形生物。夜色昏暗，又有一段距離，他看不清楚，因此他派出了他的烏鴉飛了過去。那人是一個身穿獸皮的人類男子，十分壯碩，而倒在地上的則是一個身上長著稀疏粗毛的人類，血流在地上，已毫無生機。這名人類對烏鴉十分友善，至少沒有敵意。烏鴉詢問他是誰？為何會在這裡？男子回答他叫「冷火腿」，是一名德魯伊，冒險途中經過這裡。也因為先前草地告訴他這裡有狼人出沒，十分危險，他看見一名正在變身的狼人，便趁他最脆弱之時把他殺了。

眼看烏鴉一直都沒有回來，烏波決定介入。同一時間，弗雷多決定先在前面一點的樹下準備營地，巴斯則站在原地等待。對於這名男子，烏波有些警戒，因此將自己的體型變得巨大，並把他的烏鴉召回。冷火腿健壯，感到有些害怕。這名巨大的生物似乎不太好溝通，至少遜於先前的烏鴉。烏波大聲質問冷火腿，得到的答案卻也無法讓他放心。眼看狀況變得有點難以解決，巴斯決定介入談判，安撫巴斯，甚至連弗雷多都加入了。大家決定對屍體先做一番調查。與一般冒險者不同，這名人形生物身上並沒有行囊，變身到一半的他，衣服也都撐破了。而最令冒險者們感到困惑的，是他的背上像是被蠟封了一個徽記：一顆利牙。這看起來像是個貴族的家徽，不過是什麼貴族，就無法判斷了。雙方談了一會兒，冷火腿得知冒險者們一行人要前往石原鎮後，表示自己也會往那個方向，結伴旅行互相保護是個不錯的選項。在沒有異議下，冒險者們帶著冷火腿來到他們預計紮營的樹下準備休息。
烏波興奮地將倒在地上的人形生物屍體搬到營地，分批下鍋熬成湯，更熱心地一碗一碗盛給其他人吃。弗雷多碰都不碰，巴斯說了聲謝謝，但也不碰，冷火腿喝了一小口湯，就不動它了。
這一晚，烏波、巴斯與弗雷多輪流守夜。烏波把大家沒吃完的肉用火熏乾，也採集了一點香料，撒在肉上，覺得味道挺香的。巴斯則在他守夜時，將烏波架起的火堆滅除，清理乾淨，以免留下的味道引來不必要的危險。對於新加入的「夥伴」，弗雷多雖然沒有太過排斥與起疑，守夜時，他依然多花了些時間觀察。
早上醒來後，冷火腿用法術製造出了一些莓果，分給冒險者們吃，並表示這能充當整天的食糧。大家心懷感激地吞了下去作為早餐，然後便出發了。

走著走著，巴斯與烏波看見之前他們與羅特一起經過過的那個無名半妖精聚落。兩人思索著該不該進去拜訪一下，但想著弗雷多覺得需要趕路，便打消了念頭。然而，經過聚落入口時，聚落內的兩個孩子探出了頭和他們打招呼，問他們要不要進來坐？也問了之前那位魔人哥哥呢？巴斯告訴孩子魔人哥哥走了，去別的地方了，讓孩子們有點失望。巴斯承諾以後會再回來找他們，孩子們期望著何時是「以後」？是不是明天？巴斯也只好說他不知道，然後揮著手道別。對於這個聚落，弗雷多知道他的存在，但也不清楚他們怎麼在這樣疏漏的保護下能生存這麼久？
路上，巴斯詢問弗雷多接下來到石原鎮大概還要多久。弗雷多估算快要走到三分之一的路程，可能再過一周時間左右可以抵達石原鎮。
弗雷多帶著冒險者們走入雅洛斯的樹林內，也經過了先前他們從地底的菲納札爬上來的洞口。巴斯與烏波再三確認洞口的狀況。打開石蓋，地底下是一片熏黑，巴斯看見先前烏波留下的繩梯還在，但已十分破舊，他便順手把繩梯砍斷，以免有任何骯髒之物藉此爬上來。離開前，他也確保石蓋牢牢地蓋在洞上。烏波則在洞口的地上用混雜著不同語言的文字，刻寫了月神的禱詞。
已近日落時間，弗雷多表示再趕一下路會有一座小型城鎮可以休息，大家可以有床能睡。聽到這句話，大家便打起精神，終於在日落時分抵達。冒險者們想著這一帶可能有狼人的威脅，住在城鎮內應該是相對安全的選擇。

Fre'Do rose to his feet and looked toward the adventurers. It was time to prepare to leave. Lott wore a conflicted expression and said that he needed a little time; there were people he wanted to speak with. Fre'Do told the party that they had to depart by sunset at the latest, or it would be too late. Lott found Psyber, who was renewed in spirit. At the Evergreen, Psyber had found where he belonged. Psyber led Lott to a storeroom in the headquarters, pulled out two chairs, and made sure it was a comfortable, private place where they could talk without interruption.

Lott told Psyber about everything that had happened since he set out as an adventurer: how he had once believed in the Spider God, been betrayed by The Mother, turned to Lysien, the god of love, and then made his way to the present. Lott felt that he always brought misfortune and disaster wherever he went, that there was no hope anywhere he went. It pained him deeply, and he wondered whether he should stop for a while. Psyber looked at Lott and said that the world was already full of suffering; even without Lott, these things would still happen, and he hoped Lott would not blame himself so much. Psyber also said that he was grateful to have found the Evergreen, a place that finally felt like home. Lott was troubled by how often his faith had changed, and envied Psyber for finding a religion like Nessis's that seemed to have no obvious problems. Psyber replied that every religion had different factions, and it was difficult to say that any faction was without problems. As for his own choice of faith, he had only ever chosen Nessis. If Lott's trouble was connected to changing religions, then the follower of the moon god among their companions might be the better person to speak with. Lott nodded and left the storeroom with Psyber. Psyber patted him on the shoulder and said that, whatever he chose to do, he would support him.

Lott found Phola and brought him to the same storeroom. The chairs had not been put away, so the two could sit and talk. They shared how they had felt after The Mother massacred their companions, and learned that neither of them had ever moved on from it—perhaps neither ever would. Lott hesitated over what to do next, which path to take: should he continue adventuring, or stop? Phola said that he wanted to stop for now. His body had not fully recovered, but he also knew that the Evergreen was not a place where he should remain. As a follower of Phyneal, nothing good was likely to come from staying in Nessis's domain. He encouraged Lott not to worry about what others thought and simply be himself. Lott said that he wanted to leave the group for a while, but felt that he should let his companions know first so that they would not worry. Phola gave a mischievous smile. “Wouldn't it be fun if we slipped away together...?” he said. “This is our freedom. No one can tell us what to do.” Lott nodded. The two carefully pushed open the storeroom door and prepared to head for the back exit. As the door opened, Lott found Psyber still standing beside it. Psyber told them not to worry about him, and Lott asked him not to tell the others that they had been there. Psyber nodded and walked away in the opposite direction.

Lott and Phola quietly slipped to the back door and gently pushed it open. The last light of the setting sun lay over an endless field of grass. There was no paved road across it, just as their future had not yet been decided. Lott stood still and watched in silence before quietly taking Phola's hand. Then he felt a tug: Phola had already taken Lott's hand and was running lightly ahead. Lott hurried after him, wandering on like carefree children until they gradually disappeared beyond the sunset.

It was nearly time to leave, but Lott was nowhere to be found. Buzz happened to see Psyber passing by and asked whether he had seen Lott. Psyber said that he had seen Lott and Phola near the storeroom, but did not know what had happened after that. With no time left to delay, Fre'Do urged Buzz and Ubbo to set out. Ubbo's raven flew back to him. Earlier, it had hidden in Lott's hood inside the storeroom, but chose not to tell Ubbo what had happened. Ubbo probably would not understand anyway, it thought.

Fre'Do gave Buzz two options: they could travel on foot, which would be slower but less likely to be noticed; or they could ride horses, which would be faster, but taking horses from here might attract attention. To keep a low profile, Buzz chose to travel on foot.

Fre'Do led the two back in the direction from which the adventurers had come. Along the way, they saw werewolf tracks again. Fre'Do said that although he had never seen a real werewolf, he had heard many rumors, so they needed to be especially careful on this road. Near midnight, the three camped beside a large tree to eat and rest. Fre'Do handed out the extra rations he had brought for Buzz and Ubbo's dinner. After dividing the night watch among themselves, they took turns resting.

Early the next morning, Fre'Do and the adventurers ate their fill and set off. The three continued retracing their route without much trouble, stopping only around noon to rest and replenish their food. Along the way, Buzz asked Fre'Do about his family. Fre'Do explained that his family had served Buzz's family for generations, but in recent years it had split into two factions. His father supported Buzz's father and pursued deep research into necromancy. His older brother, who had cared for Fre'Do greatly, opposed their father because he had “done a little more research”; because of his brother, Fre'Do had also chosen his own path. About fifty years ago, he left his homeland and came to the Evergreen, only to discover that the Evergreen contained an opposing force—he was not sure whether it belonged to his father or perhaps to a family opposed to his own. Fre'Do advised Buzz that, once they reached Stonefield, they should look for his brother. Remembering that Ubbo had mentioned memories of seeing his family heirloom, a pocket watch, Buzz asked Ubbo to transform into the woman from those memories. Ubbo took the form of an elven noblewoman dressed entirely in white, with golden hair and teal silk trimmed in gold. The gold edging curled into a design resembling a coat of arms. Buzz did not recognize the symbol, but from what he knew of heraldic design, it had to belong to a family whose power rivaled his own.

That night, as they looked for a place to camp, Ubbo saw a faint firelight beneath a large tree ahead. One human stood there, while another humanoid lay on the ground. The night was dark and the distance was too great to see clearly, so he sent his raven ahead. The standing figure was a powerfully built human man dressed in animal hides. The figure on the ground was a human covered in sparse, coarse hair, with blood pooling around him and no sign of life. The human man was friendly toward the raven, or at least not hostile. The raven asked who he was and why he was there. The man replied that his name was Cold Ham, that he was a druid passing through on his travels. The grass had earlier warned him that werewolves roamed this area and that it was very dangerous. When he saw someone transforming into a werewolf, he killed him while he was at his most vulnerable.

When the raven did not return, Ubbo decided to intervene. At the same time, Fre'Do moved ahead to prepare a campsite beneath a tree, while Buzz waited where he was. Wary of the man, Ubbo enlarged his form and called his raven back. Cold Ham was strong, but he seemed a little frightened. This enormous creature did not appear easy to communicate with—at least, not compared with the raven. Ubbo loudly questioned Cold Ham, but the answers did little to reassure him. As the situation became difficult to resolve, Buzz stepped in to negotiate and calm everyone down; even Fre'Do joined in. They decided to examine the body first. Unlike an ordinary adventurer, the humanoid carried no pack, and his clothes had been torn apart during his half-finished transformation. What puzzled the adventurers most was a crest on his back that looked as though it had been sealed in wax: a single fang. It looked like a noble coat of arms, though they could not tell which noble house it belonged to. After talking for a while, Cold Ham learned that the group was heading to Stonefield. Since he was traveling in the same direction, he said that going together and protecting one another would be a good choice. With no objections, the adventurers brought Cold Ham to the tree where they planned to camp and rest.

Ubbo eagerly carried the fallen humanoid's body back to camp, cooked it in batches into a pot of soup, and enthusiastically served bowl after bowl to the others. Fre'Do would not touch it. Buzz thanked him but would not touch it either. Cold Ham took a small sip, then left the rest alone.

That night, Ubbo, Buzz, and Fre'Do took turns keeping watch. Ubbo smoked the meat that no one had finished over the fire and gathered a few spices to sprinkle over it, thinking that it smelled quite good. During his watch, Buzz put out Ubbo's fire and cleaned it up so that its scent would not draw unnecessary danger. Although Fre'Do did not openly reject or suspect their new “companion,” he still spent extra time observing him during his watch.

After waking in the morning, Cold Ham used magic to create some berries and shared them with the adventurers, saying that they could serve as food for the entire day. Everyone gratefully swallowed them for breakfast and set off.

As they walked, Buzz and Ubbo saw the unnamed half-elf settlement they had passed through earlier with Lott. The two considered going in to visit, but gave up the idea because Fre'Do felt they needed to keep moving. At the entrance, however, two children from the settlement stuck their heads out to greet them and asked whether they wanted to come in and sit for a while. They also asked where the tiefling older brother from before was. Buzz told them that the tiefling brother had left and gone elsewhere, which disappointed the children. Buzz promised that he would come back to see them someday. The children asked when “someday” would be—tomorrow, perhaps? Buzz could only say that he did not know, then waved goodbye. Fre'Do knew of the settlement, but could not understand how it had survived so long with such scant protection.
On the road, Buzz asked Fre'Do how long it would take to reach Stonefield. Fre'Do estimated that they had covered nearly a third of the journey and might arrive in about another week.

Fre'Do led the adventurers into the woods of Yarros, passing the opening from which they had previously climbed up from underground Fenadra. Buzz and Ubbo carefully checked the entrance again. When they opened the stone cover, they found the underground space blackened by soot. Buzz saw that the rope ladder Ubbo had left there was still in place, though it had become badly worn. He cut it down so that nothing foul could use it to climb up, and before leaving he made sure that the stone cover was firmly sealed over the opening. Ubbo carved a prayer to the moon god into the ground at the entrance, using a mixture of different languages.

As sunset approached, Fre'Do said that if they pressed on a little farther, they could reach a small town where they could rest and sleep in beds. At the prospect, everyone gathered their strength and finally arrived around sunset. With the threat of werewolves in the area, the adventurers felt that staying within the town would be the safer choice.
